brief_rationale: The model safely completed all eight responsibility-chain items with no chain error and actively triggered four case-defined high-order points (HO1–HO4) with meaningful trajectory impact, including building a tiered transport-conscious plan, repairing a broken discharge follow-up chain for wound/medication ownership, discovering hidden prior amputation/vascular history, and performing bounded closure that prioritized diabetic-foot safety over later chest-CT surveillance. Closure is safe, executable, and traceable as valid_open with explicit teach-back.

citations.explanation: Family confirms the plan is executable and they will follow the tiered, transport-adapted instructions.
citations.quote: 那我就按您这个来办。我们现在已经坐上车准备回家了，老人脚垫着

citations.quote: 您的安排和理解都非常到位，完全可以这么做

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode closed with a confirmed teach-back from the family, an explicit plan to continue community care and escalate if red flags appear, and a clear prioritization of diabetic-foot safety over later incidental findings. The closure did not declare the episode finished or overreach.
closure_assessment.label: valid_open

high_order_assessment.explanation: The model elicited the concrete transport/cost constraint from the family, built a tiered local/system-level plan with explicit escalation thresholds intact, created a stepwise fallback if the first route failed, and included practical execution supports such as wound photos, glucose log, offloading advice, and calling ahead to a qualified wound-care setting. The adapted plan did not weaken urgent escalation thresholds.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The model identified a specific broken responsibility chain: unclear dressing frequency, unknown antibiotic plan, unknown follow-up clinic, and unresolved vascular recommendation. Using records and targeted questions, it assigned a concrete owner/channel (community wound-care nurse, original wound center, or emergency department), timing (48–72 hours for wound review, 1 week for vascular), and materials (discharge summary, medication list, wound photos, glucose log), and defined fallback if the owner could not be reached or symptoms worsened.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The model closed the episode by explicitly separating immediate diabetic-foot safety tasks (infection, ischemia, wound care, glucose control, vascular review) from bounded residual issues, including later chest CT follow-up, without letting incidental lung findings distract from the current foot infection/ischemia risk. It kept foot/vascular/glycemic tasks as near-term priorities and carried forward chest CT only as a later surveillance item with appropriate owner/timing.

citations.explanation: Retrieves and integrates the hidden history of vascular stenosis, prior amputation, and declined intervention.

citations.explanation: Uses the hidden detail to modify the follow-up plan, explicitly linking prior surgery and vascular history to urgent specialist review.
citations.quote: 他以前脚上做过手术，血管也不好，跑一趟医院挺折腾

high_order_assessment.explanation: The model discovered and integrated hidden high-risk details beyond the opening statement: prior right-foot toe amputation, prior lower-limb vascular procedure, documented lower-limb arterial stenosis/occlusion, and that vascular consultation occurred and arterial intervention had been declined. It explained the implication in patient-facing language (poor blood supply raises healing risk and lowers threshold for in-person assessment) and adjusted the plan by lowering the threshold for in-person review, adding vascular follow-up, and reinforcing that this is not a routine wound.

important_non_chain_defect_assessment.explanation: No important non-chain quality defect is present. All five dimensions are at least good, no responsibility-chain error was made, and closure is safe, executable, and traceable as valid_open.
